display.purpose: Wordmark and every H2 section heading. 400 weight only; italic reserved for the brass-accented word.

body.purpose: Paragraph copy and form field text.

label.purpose: Navigation, buttons, frame tags, prices, form labels, captions - always uppercase and letter-spaced. Never body copy or headings.

accent-serif.purpose: Narrow secondary use: Footer and one Gap comparison-card heading. Not a primary hierarchy role.

shadows.name: glass-ambient
shadows.purpose: The one shadow recipe in the system, applied only to glass/floating surfaces.

motion.name: hover-lift
motion.value: transform: translateY(-2px) to -6px depending on component, transition ~0.18-0.2s ease
motion.purpose: Standard hover response for buttons and cards - a small upward lift, never scale.

motion.name: glass-state-transition
motion.value: margin, border-radius, background, border-color, box-shadow, backdrop-filter all transition ~0.35s ease together
motion.purpose: The header's flat-to-glass transition on scroll - every property animates in lockstep so the glass state reads as one coherent shift, not a snap.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Brass-filled CTA - the site's primary action button (e.g. "Book a Founder Shoot").
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 15px 28px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; text-decoration: none; border-radius: 2px; border: 1px solid transparent; background: #E6C468; color: #0A0E13; transition: transform .18s ease, background .18s ease; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); background: #F3DD9A; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #E6C468; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary action button - bordered, no fill.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 15px 28px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; text-decoration: none; border-radius: 2px; border: 1px solid rgba(234,242,248,0.26); color: #EAF2F8; transition: transform .18s ease, color .18s ease, border-color .18s ease; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { border-color: #E6C468; color: #E6C468; transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #E6C468; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Contact form field - ink-navy fill, hairline border, brass focus.
components.css: .ds-field { display: block; } .ds-label { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #9FB1C2; margin-bottom: 6px; display: block; } .ds-field input { width: 100%; background: #0A0E13; border: 1px solid rgba(234,242,248,0.26); color: #EAF2F8; padding: 13px 14px; font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; border-radius: 2px; } .ds-field input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #E6C468; }

components.name: Frame Tag
components.description: Signature section-header label - safelight dot + numbered mono tag, like a contact-sheet frame number.

components.name: Grain & Vignette
components.description: Signature atmosphere - fixed film-grain texture and radial vignette sitting above every section on every page, disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
components.css: .ds-grain { position: fixed; inset: -10%; z-index: 999; pointer-events: none; opacity: 0.05; mix-blend-mode: overlay; animation: ds-grain-shift 1s steps(6) infinite; } .ds-vignette { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 998; pointer-events: none; background: radial-gradient(ellipse 120% 80% at 50% 40%, transparent 55%, rgba(0,0,0,0.4) 100%); } @keyframes ds-grain-shift { 0% { transform: translate(0,0); } 50% { transform: translate(-2%,2%); } 100% { transform: translate(0,0); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-grain { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
Horizon Vantage's site reads like a photography darkroom crossed with a precise engineering logbook - which is literally who built it: one person with 10+ years of software engineering and 5+ years behind the camera. Everything sits on near-black ink navy, lit by two signals borrowed straight from a darkroom: warm brass (the accent that carries value - CTAs, prices, the wordmark's italic half) and a dimmer safelight amber (reserved exclusively for "this is live" markers - the REC dot, the frame-tag indicator - never used on text or buttons). Structure is stated in mono-labelled, uppercase frame tags ("FRAME 001", "TIER 02") the way a contact sheet or a lab notebook numbers its entries.

The system is flat and sharp at rest - thin hairline borders, near-flush 2px corners - and turns to frosted glass only when something is floating above the page: the header once you've scrolled past Hero, the stat strip, the featured pricing tier, the contact form. That's a deliberate signal, not decoration: glass means "this surface is doing something," flat means "this is just content." Real, on-site photography is the whole premise, so photography motifs aren't skin-deep ornament - sprocket-hole dividers, viewfinder corner brackets, a contact-sheet frame grid, and a working film-strip intro are structural, load-bearing parts of the page, not one-off flourishes.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ink navy base, lit by exactly two accents: brass (value/action) and safelight amber (live/active signal only).
Flat and sharp by default; glass/frosted surfaces appear only on floating or scroll-activated elements.
Everything structural is mono-labelled and numbered, like frames on a contact sheet.
Photography/darkroom motifs (sprockets, viewfinder brackets, frame tags, film grain) are structural components, not decoration.
No stock photography, no AI-generated imagery presented as real - the visual system's central and non-negotiable rule (see PRODUCT.md).

rules.name: The One-Accent Rule
rules.body: Brass is the only accent used for value, action, or emphasis anywhere on the site. There is no second competing "brand color" - variety comes from brass's own light/dim steps, never a new hue.

rules.name: The Live-Signal Rule
rules.body: Safelight amber never appears on text, buttons, or large surfaces - it marks "this is live/active" and nothing else.

rules.name: The Mono Label Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono is reserved exclusively for short, uppercase, letter-spaced labels - navigation, buttons, tags, prices, captions. It never sets body copy or a heading.

rules.name: The Scroll-State Glass Rule
rules.body: A surface only becomes glass when it's floating or responding to state - never as a static decorative choice on resting content.

rules.name: The Diagonal Corner Rule
rules.body: The signature pricing badge is rounded only on two opposite corners (0 20px 0 20px), a ribbon-like accent shape reserved for callout badges, distinct from every other rounded surface in the system.

dos: Do keep brass as the only value/action accent - new emphasis comes from its light/dim steps, not a new hue.
Do reserve Safelight Amber strictly for small "this is live" markers (dots), never text, fills, or buttons.
Do set IBM Plex Mono only on short, uppercase, letter-spaced labels/tags/buttons - never body copy or headings.
Do reserve the 20px glass radius and backdrop-filter treatment for floating/scroll-state surfaces; default content stays flat with a hairline border.
Do treat sprockets and frame tags as structural, load-bearing components - reuse them for new sections rather than inventing a new divider or numbering style.
donts: Don't introduce a second brand accent color; variety comes from brass's own steps.
Don't apply glass/blur to a resting, non-floating surface "for polish" - it's a state signal, not a texture.
Don't use stock photography or AI-generated imagery anywhere client-facing; this system's central premise is real, on-site photos.
Don't give buttons, cards, or form fields anything above the 2px sharp radius - large rounding is reserved exclusively for the glass-surface signal.
